item.text:
Chapter 6B research is complete for Joe Biden, United States, 2022 only. No score was assigned.

The evidence shows substantial welfare-oriented legislation and delivery in health insurance, rental aid, water infrastructure, and future Medicare protections. Outcomes were mixed: insurance coverage improved, but food insecurity and supplemental poverty—especially child poverty—worsened sharply amid inflation and expiration of temporary supports. Audits found major administrative and measurement weaknesses. Federal attribution is strongest for legislation, executive guidance, and federally administered programs, but weaker for nationwide outcomes mediated by Congress, states, localities, markets, and the pandemic.

## Evidence dossier

### Newly accepted units

### Verified reused evidence

These were reopened and verified but are not newly discovered documents:

- E014: GAO found that CDC, HRSA, and FEMA used racial/ethnic population data, outreach, translation, extended hours, and pop-up clinics to target underserved groups, while available comparisons still showed disparities. Locator: “Fast Facts” and “What GAO Found,” lines 264–281. [GAO-22-105079](https://www.gao.gov/products/gao-22-105079)

- E015: CDC’s 2022 NHIS found only 22.8% of adults current on the composite set of age-appropriate vaccinations; coverage was 12.1% among Black adults and 17.0% among Hispanic adults versus 26.1% among White adults. Locator: lines 67–68 and 112–115. [CDC AdultVaxView](https://www.cdc.gov/adultvaxview/publications-resources/adult-vaccination-coverage-2022.html)

- E016: Among children aged six months to four years, 10.1% had received a COVID-19 vaccine dose and 5.1% had completed the series by December 31, 2022; first-dose coverage ranged from 2.1% to 36.1% across jurisdictions and was much lower in rural counties. Locator: Summary and Results, lines 65–70. [CDC MMWR](https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/72/wr/mm7207a4.htm)

- E017: The Commonwealth Fund’s 2022 survey documented extensive underinsurance and cost barriers despite nominal coverage, with burdens concentrated among lower-income, Black, and Hispanic adults. Locator: “Survey Findings,” figures 4–7 and “Affordability Is the Biggest Problem.” [Commonwealth Fund](https://www.commonwealthfund.org/publications/issue-briefs/2022/sep/state-us-health-insurance-2022-biennial-survey)

E018 was verified as useful implementation context but not retained as a separate claim because it substantially duplicates E014’s federal/community partnership evidence.

## Lens coverage

| Lens | Coverage |
|---|---|
| 6B.1 | Marketplace subsidies, Medicare legislation, water investment, and equity-directed implementation show revealed welfare priority; official promotional claims alone were not treated as proof. |
| 6B.2 | Strong coverage across health insurance, affordability, food security, rental assistance, homelessness, water, and social protection. Education evidence was thinner because the prominent 2022 debt-cancellation initiative was not delivered during the period. |
| 6B.3 | Vaccine targeting, low-income Marketplace subsidies, disadvantaged-community water rules, rental eligibility, and subgroup outcomes cover vulnerable groups. |
| 6B.4 | GAO audits provide strong evidence of professional federal oversight alongside incomplete data, local-capacity constraints, and major payment-control weaknesses. |
| 6B.5 | Census, CDC, USDA, CMS, and HUD measurement systems are extensive; GAO found significant gaps in ERA and emergency-relief measurement and correction. |
| 6B.6 | Marketplace support, vaccination, and rental aid mitigated pandemic suffering; rising food insecurity and child poverty are substantial contrary outcomes. |
| 6B.7 | No substantiated target-period evidence was located that the Biden federal executive conditioned ordinary welfare on personal or partisan loyalty. This is a residual evidentiary gap, not proof that no isolated abuse occurred. Eligibility, state variation, and administrative burdens persisted but are analytically distinct from loyalty punishment. |
| 6B.8 | Equity targeting and affordability provisions support dignity/equal-opportunity aims; racial, rural, income, insurance, and state disparities show incomplete realization. |
| 6B.9 | The IRA’s statutory Medicare machinery and five-year infrastructure appropriations are the strongest durability evidence. Temporary tax credits, finite subsidy extensions, and emergency programs were less durable. |
| 6B.10 | Mixed: insurance access improved, but real median income fell, food insecurity rose, SPM poverty increased, and child SPM poverty more than doubled. Later-starting statutory benefits cannot be counted as realized 2022 life chances. |

- Search modes used: broad welfare outcomes, institution/archive, program-specific, adverse/contrary, legal-authority, equity, and loyalty/conditionality searches. English is the relevant local administrative language.

The read-only workspace and unavailable local shell prevented inspection or modification of `research-ledger-manifest.json`. The eight `SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON` records above are the deterministic manifest delta; I cannot honestly manufacture a cumulative manifest without access to its prior entries.

Another 6B-specific wave would probably have limited marginal value for the overall chapter. It could still improve two narrow gaps: realized 2022 education outcomes beyond debt-relief announcements, and affirmative evidence concerning political nonconditionality under 6B.7. It is unlikely to change the main mixed finding unless it uncovers stronger causal evaluations separating Biden-era federal action from inflation, congressional expiration decisions, and state implementation.
